title: Serine hydrolases designed from scratch
summary: RFdiffusion backbones and the PLACER network for catalytic-cycle ensembles produced de novo serine hydrolases with kcat/Km up to 4.3e3 M^-1 s^-1 and crystal structures within 1 Å of the designs, in five folds not seen in this enzyme family. Design success rates not checked.
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design and UCLA

evidence.tested: De novo designed serine hydrolases characterized experimentally: best catalytic efficiency about 2.2 x 10^5 M^-1 s^-1, and crystal structures within 1 Angstrom of the design models in five new folds.
evidence.unknown: The abstract states no limitations; design success rates were not checked in the text read.
evidence.ai_role: RFdiffusion generated enzyme backbones from active-site descriptions; an ensemble-generation method (PLACER) assessed active-site preorganization across the reaction.
